BOP analytical summary

Ellie Knott

2026-10-22

Support for Domestic Politicians

Sandu remains more popular than Sor or Dodon, especially after 2023. Support for Sandu has decreased, while support for Dodon and Sor has declined.

Those identifying as Romanian are more supportive of Sandu. Those with a high level of education are more supportive of Sandu. Those who worry about corruption and war are more supportive of Sandu. Those who support unification are more supportive of Sandu. Those who support EU membership are more supportive of Sandu.

Those who identify as Russian or Ukrainian, or complete the survey in Russian, are less supportive of Sandu. Those who reside in Gagauzia are less supportive of Sandu. Those who support Putin are less supportive of Sandu.

Those who think Moldova is heading in a good direction are more supportive of Sandu and Dodon.

Those who identify as Gagauz, Russia, Ukrainian or Bulgarian are more supportive of Dodon and Sor. Those with a lower socioeconomic level are more supportive of Dodon and Sor. Those who reside in the south are more supportive of Dodon and Sor. Those who are more supportive of Putin are more supportive of Dodon and Sor.

Those with a lower level of education are more supportive of Dodon. Those who name as an important media source are more supportive of Dodon.

Those who complete the survey in Russian are more supportive of Sor. Those who reside in the centre and north are more supportive of Sor.

Those who complete the survey in Russian or a higher level of education are less supportive of Dodon. Those who support EU membership and unification are less supportive of Dodon.

Those who worry about corrupption are less supportive of Dodon and Sor.

Those who reside in rural areas are less supportive of Sor.

  • Age & gender: not significant
  • Ethnicity:
    • Romanian: significant for Sandu (+)
    • Russian: significant for Dodon & Sor (+) and Sandu (-)
    • Ukrainian: significant for Dodon & Sor (+) and Sandu (-)
    • Gagauz: (only) significant for Dodon (+)
    • Bulgarian: significant for Dodon & Sor (+)
    • Language of questionnaire: Russian significant for Sor (+) and Sandu and Dodon (-)
  • Education:
    • Low: significant for Dodon (+)
    • High: significant for Sandu (+) and Dodon (-)
  • Socioeconomic:
    • Low: significant for Dodon and Sor (+)
    • High: not significant

Geography

  • Macro region: centre & north significant for Sor (+); others not significant
    • South: significant for Sor (+) and Dodon (-)
    • Gagauzia: significant for Sandu (-)
  • Ecology: rural significant for Sor (-)

Attitudes

  • Media: TV significant for Dodon (+); others not sigificant; internet not significant
  • Direction: good significant for Sandu and Dodon (+) and Sor (-)
  • Worries:
    • Poverty & interethnic relations: not significant
    • Corruption: significant for Sandu (+) and Dodon and Sor (-)
    • War: significant for Sandu (+); not significant for others
  • Unification: in favour significant for Sandu (+) and Dodon (-); not significant for Sor
  • Support for Putin: significant for Sandu (-) and Dodon and Sor (+)
  • EU membership: significant for Sandu (+) and Dodon (-); not significant for Sor

Support for International Politicians

Support for Zelenskyy and Putin has declined over time. Zelenskyy remains less popular and has continued to decline over time, while support for Putin increased slightly in 2025.

More educated and better off people, and those identifying as Romanian or completing the questionnaire in Romanian are more supportive of Zelenskyy. Those residing in Gagauzia are less supportive of Putin. Those supporting EU membership and unification are more supportive of Zelenskyy. Those worried about war are more supportive of Zelenskyy.

More educated and better off are less supportive of Putin, as are those identifying as Romania.

Those identifying as Russian, Ukrainian, Gagauz and Bulgarian, and completing the survey in Russian, are more supportive of Putin. Those residing in Gagauzia as more supportive of Putin. Those supporting EU membership and unification as less supportive of Putin. Those worried about war and corruption as less supportive of Putin.

  • Gender: woman significant for Putin (-)
  • Ethnicity:

    • Russian, Ukrainian, Gagauz, Bulgarian: significant for Putin (+); not significant for Zelenskyy
  • Russian questionnaire: significant for Putin (+) and Zelenskyy (-)
  • Education: low not significant; high significant for Zelenskyy (+) and Putin (-)
  • Socioeconomic: low significant for Putin (+) and high significant for Zelenskyy (+) and Putin (-)

Geography

  • Region:
    • Gagauzia: significant for Putin (+) and Zelenskyy (-)
    • Centre & North: significant for Putin (+); south not significant
  • Ecology: not significant

Attitudes

  • Worries:
    • Poverty: significant in support for Zelenskyy (-)
    • Corruption: significant in support for Putin (-)
    • War: significant in support for Zelenskyy (+) and Putin (-)
  • EU membership: significant in support for Zelenskyy (+) and Putin (-)
  • Unification: significant in support for Zelenskyy (+) and Putin (-)

Unification

Support for unification as rising over time: from 21% in 2017 to over 35% in 2025.

Those supporting EU membership and NATO membership as more likely to support unification. Those identifying as Romanian as more likely to support unification.

Demographics

  • Age & gender: not significant
  • Ethnicity:
    • Romanian: significant (+)
    • Russian, Ukrainian, Gagauz, Bulgarian: significant (-)
  • Russian questionnaire: significant (-)
  • Education: low (+); high not consistently significant
  • Socioeconomic: not significant

Geography

  • Nothing consistently significant

Attitudes

  • Direction: good as significant (+)
  • Worries: poverty and interethnic relations are not significant
    • Corruption: significant (+)
    • War: significant (+)
  • EU membership: significant (+)
  • NATO membership: significant (+)

International Organisations

Those supporting joining the Eurasian Union are older, and more likely Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, or Gagauz. They are more likely to answer the questionnaire in Russia and be poorer. Those supporting it are more likely to live in Gaguazia or the North, and in urban areas. They are more likely to be concerned about poverty. Those naming TV and the internet are important sources of media are more likely to support joining.

Those with a high level of education or concerned about corruption are less likely to support joining the Eurasia Union Those thinking that Moldova is going in a good direction are less likely to support it.

Those who identify as Romanian are more likely to support joining the EU and NATO. Those with a high level of education are more likely to support joining the EU, while those with a high socioeconomic level are more likely to support joining the EU and NATO. Those residing in rural areas are more likely to support joining the EU. Those who think Moldova is heading in a good direction are more likely to support joining the EU and NATO.

Those concernd about corruption and war are more likely to support joining the EU and NATO.

Those residing in the South are less likely to support joining NATO but more likely to support joining the EU.

Those answering the questionnaire in Russian are less likely to support joining the EU and NATO. Those residing in Gagauzia are less likely to support joining the EU, and those residing in central and northern regions are less likely to support joining the EU and NATO. Those concerned about inter-ethnic relations are less likely to support joining the EU.
